items.stem: The 'service-recovery paradox' describes how a customer can end up more loyal when:

options.text: A problem never occurs at all
options.rationale: The paradox is specifically about recovery after a failure.

options.text: A problem is resolved quickly and well after it occurs
options.rationale: Correct: excellent recovery can leave a customer more loyal than if nothing had gone wrong.

options.text: The company blames the customer for the issue
The complaint is ignored to avoid conflict

items.explanation: Correct: excellent recovery can leave a customer more loyal than if nothing had gone wrong.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Customer Effort Score (CES) is most appropriate for measuring:

options.text: Overall emotional loyalty to the brand
options.rationale: That is closer to what NPS attempts to capture.

options.text: How easy it was to get a specific task done
options.rationale: Correct: CES captures the effort required for a specific interaction.
CES is a customer metric, not a financial one.

options.text: How many features a product has
options.rationale: Feature count is unrelated to effort score.

items.explanation: Correct: CES captures the effort required for a specific interaction.

items.stem: Which TWO make a customer journey map genuinely useful? (Select TWO)

options.text: It captures the customer's emotions at each step
options.rationale: Correct: emotions reveal where the experience succeeds or fails.

options.text: It is built from real customer research, not assumptions
options.rationale: Correct: grounding the map in research keeps it honest.

options.text: It documents only internal system steps
options.rationale: An internal-process view misses the customer's experience.

options.text: It is drawn once and never revisited
options.rationale: A static map quickly goes stale.

items.explanation: Correct: emotions reveal where the experience succeeds or fails.; Correct: grounding the map in research keeps it honest.
